headline: Musk's Grok chatbot advised Trump on capturing Venezuela's president, report says
summary: A source told Time magazine that the AI suggested Maduro was unpopular and his capture would be celebrated, influencing Trump's actions.
details: A report from Time magazine details a secret meeting in December 2025 between former President Trump and Elon Musk, where Trump reportedly spent hours interacting with Musk's AI chatbot, Grok.

During their conversation, Trump allegedly asked Grok how Venezuelans would react to the capture of their president, Nicolás Maduro. The AI reportedly responded that Maduro was a "deeply unpopular dictator" and that his downfall would be "celebrated."

This alleged interaction occurred months after Trump had begun ordering U.S. military strikes against Venezuelan boats, which he claimed were involved in drug trafficking. Grok's assessment of public sentiment in Venezuela may have influenced Trump's perspective.
Following an alleged U.S. invasion in January 2026, which resulted in Maduro's capture, Trump reportedly viewed Grok as "ingenious," according to a source cited by Time.
The report also notes that Grok has been utilized by the Pentagon. The military's head of AI stated that Gov Grok was used to deploy and strike targets during the Iran War in June of this year.

While other AI models from companies like OpenAI and Anthropic are also used by the Department of Defense, Grok's role could expand. Musk and Palmer Luckey have been appointed to co-lead a Pentagon study on the use of advanced technology in battlefields.

This alleged interaction occurred months after Trump had begun ordering U.S. military strikes against Venezuelan boats, which he claimed were involved in drug trafficking. Grok's assessment of public sentiment in Venezuela may have influenced Trump's perspective.

Following an alleged U.S. invasion in January 2026, which resulted in Maduro's capture, Trump reportedly viewed Grok as "ingenious," according to a source cited by Time.

The report also notes that Grok has been utilized by the Pentagon. The military's head of AI stated that Gov Grok was used to deploy and strike targets during the Iran War in June of this year.

headline: Kevin Mandia's Armadin raises $255.5M for AI-era security
summary: The cybersecurity veteran's new startup, Armadin, secured over $445M in total funding at a $2.5B valuation by using 'agent swarms' to test defenses.
details: Kevin Mandia, the founder of Mandiant, has launched his new cybersecurity startup, Armadin, which has already raised $255.5 million in a Series B funding round, valuing the company at over $2.5 billion. This latest round, led by Andreessen Horowitz and Accel, brings Armadin's total funding to over $445 million in just six months.

Armadin is pioneering a new approach to enterprise security by developing 'always-on agent swarms' designed for the AI era. Unlike traditional penetration testing, these agent swarms chain together vulnerabilities to simulate sophisticated attacks, aiming to identify and patch weaknesses before malicious actors can exploit them.

The company's innovative strategy is to proactively find and seal security holes by mimicking the way advanced threats, including those from rogue AI agents, might operate. This ensures organizations are better prepared against emerging cyber threats.
This significant funding underscores investor confidence in Mandia's vision and Armadin's potential to revolutionize defense testing in an increasingly complex threat landscape.
